messages.content: So far so good! NoO seems to be the same so far, need to put more time with it.
I feel that the ability to avoid obstacles at the roadside seems to be not as good as the BD V2

My experience today was really bad. I drived for 5 minutes, than changed to BD V2.
Lateral was really bad, I did not try long or NoO.
Changing lanes skipped a lane went diagonally to the next one.
Constantly driving not in the lane.
The general feeling was: I can't trust this.
Make sure your tuning is in check, especially if you are using torque lateral control. I find the models behave much different if the values aren’t correct for your car.
how should I check this? Yes I use the ML torque lateral control.

I have a ford hybrid.   Torque lateral control toggle is Grey out.  
What benefits are with that on some cars?
I have disabled NNLC and now it’s performing really well 🙂
Torque lateral control is currently not supported for Ford, due to angle control that Ford uses for lateral.
Got it.  So the reported issues with ND doesn't apply to us?
Didn’t know this page existed ! I assume each model, you’ll be making a section for?
Works great for me so far 👍
Yea, we tend to have a new forum created when there’s a new model to test.
ND seems to drive better than BDv2.  it doesnt hug the left side as much as it did before.  only did a short drive though.  so far so good for me.
Skoda Superb, CC only. With NNLC works great. Without it, it was not so good.
I refuse to drive without NNLC.. comparing ND and BDv2 this performs much better! Still needs  few improvements in lateral though.
Still has lateral issues this model
So I went back to FarmVille as it feels the most stable
With NNLC on of course
Without NNLC, torque is 💩
Does ND assist with turns? I remember bd/fv does but doesn’t seem to assist with turns on NoO?
ND has been okay, but BDv2 is more *confident* in some areas still.
I have seen some errors made by ND when changing lanes, but as for lane centering I feel more confident than BDv2. It seems that they all have some type of compromise.
BDv2 will cross the line for me.  i noticed ND will too but if the roads are narrower but does fine on LA freeways.  kinda weird that way haha
ND doesn't like stopping at stop signs for me
It usually has no issue blowing straight through
ND hugs too much to the right. Only tested on highways. Going back to Farmville.
weird, mine hugs to the left more.
lol this is crazy..
I had ND recognize a stop sign way ahead in the dark compared to other models.. also this model finally plans paths straight ahead rather than merge to the right when a lane splits.
What if you enable offsets? And either set it to auto or lanelines?
ND is so good for me.

Tried ND again in snowy city driving conditions. Lateral performs really well and seems to plan its route/trajectory better than FV when the road markings are obscured by snow. ND likes to follow the tire tracks in the snow, FV kinda does not.
I'll try tomorrow BDv2, but I think it did better job on keeping the right lane after turn. ND always oversteers a little bit.
Back to BDV2 for me
Yup, after BDv2 test, definitely I'll use it for now. The turns are way better than ND
interesting, maybe I'll stick with BDv2 for now. haven't tried ND out yet though lol
i find ND >BDv1 >BDv2 for me on a tssp
Still on ND.. haven’t switched. I’m hoping for a newer improved model soon though..
I read they’re working on a new solution for the speed in experimental mode, so probably it will take some time.

depends. the new solution is going through their driveGPT solution. idk if they're only going forward with that now or if they have a few more models they want to crank out using their current (previous?) training solutions
So ND is not driveGPT kind of training?
no. not that im aware of.

With DriveGPT I assume it wouldn't be too hard to generate training data of cars coming to full and complete stops at stop signs. These models suck with stop signs so I bet they're still using driving footage
agreed. hopefully we see drivegpt models soon

So I'm finding ND is doing the basics better than any other model I've used in my Honda Pilot.
I'd had issues with BDv1 and BDv2 where they would pull too far to the right and other cross the right road line.
They would be fine on the highway in the inside or center lane, but the outside lane would have the car too far to the right.

ND seems to do a better job of keeping centered, although from time to time I can tell it's doing a very very slow ping pong.
I've found that it takes turns very well also.
So what is the main difference between the current training and gpt. AFAIK the experimental mode is end to end model and I thought that is the GPT type of training/model.
I'd just love for the models to be trainable with my own driving style. Right now all of them drive like crazy taxi drivers in Sacramento.
They like to wait until I'm on top of a stopping car before trying  to slam on the brakes and failing.
It's strange, because for me ND starts decelerating from far away
yeah ND seems to hug a lot especially on curves (at least more noticeable at night but to be fair, its not always easy to see lane lines with the salted roads), keep having to take over a bit
Something I noticed with ND is when using MADS alone it seems to ping pong. Otherwise, i like how to navigate and try to squeeze through when theres an opening.
